EQUIPMENT REQUIRED
In this lesson, you will learn about motion transducers.
INTRODUCTIONM
You use motion transducers every time you drive a car......
The speedometer indicates how fast you are going in absolute terms, miles per hour or MPH.
A tachometer is also a motion transducer...................
It indicates relative motion, rotations per minute or RPM of the engine.
These motion transducers are normally mechanical...........
However, in newer cars, speedometers and tachometers are being replaced by electronic motion transducers.
Industries are using electronic motion transducers more and more.
Let's begin the lesson on MOTION TRANSDUCERS..............................
The LED, P1D1, is biased to remain on at all times. It is the light emitter.
If the input frequency is 4.5 kHz with a 1 V/1 kHz CF, then Eout is 4.5 volts.
What's different about the RPM circuit is the formula used to calculate velocity or the relative measurement of RPM.
Electronic motion sensors are devices that change velocity (ft/sec) into frequency (cycles/sec).
DISCUSSION
Notice that in velocity and frequency, time is common.
The motion transducers job is to change distance to cycles.
Three of the most popular electronic motion sensors are:...
The photointerrupter operates as its name implies.
The photointerrupter motion sensor is two photodevices, one is an emitter or transmitter, such as a lamp or LED.
The other is a receiver. Such as a photocell or phototransistor.
A moving object is then allowed to pass between the emitter and receiver.
The moving object is made with protrusions or holes that will make or break the light path from emitter to receiver.
When there is a path for light, the light receiver senses the energy and produces an output, usually a HIGH value.
When there is NO path for light, the light is blocked and the light receiver has a low or zero output.
In other words, the moving object interrupts or passes the light from emitter to receiver.
The HIGH to LOW transitions produce cycles that are measurable in electronic circuits.
In a photointerrupter motion sensor, if the speed of the moving object increases, what happens to the cycle output of the light receiver?
When the moving object speeds up, the making and breaking of the light path increases. This does not decrease the HIGH and LOW transitions of the light receiver's output.
TRY AGAIN!
When the moving object speeds up, the making and breaking of the light path increases. This does not cause the HIGH and LOW transitions of the light receiver to remain the same.
TRY AGAIN!
The second type of electronic motion sensor also uses light.
The photoreflector motion sensor uses two photodevices.....
One photodevice is the emitter and one is the receiver.
The difference is that both photodevices are on the same side. To the left or right of the moving object.
Again, the moving object is made with protusions or holes..
When there is a protrusion or no hole, light is reflected from the emitter to the receiver.
The light receiver senses the reflected light and produces an output, usually a HIGH value.
When there is no protrusion or a hole, the light is not reflected.
The light receiver does not sense the light and produces a zero or LOW output.
In other words, the moving object reflects or does not reflect the light to the photoreceiver.
The HIGH to LOW transitions produce cycles that are measurable in electronic circuits.
If the output of a photointerrupter sensor is HIGH, what would be the output of a photoreflector sensor for the same conditions?
The photointerrupter produces a HIGH output when there is a hole, light must pass through. The photoreflector produces a HIGH output when there is no hole, light must reflect to the receiver..
TRY AGAIN!
The last electronic motion sensor does not use light.......
The magnetic pickup motion sensor uses a permanent or electromagnet.
The magnet produces a magnetic field, recall that when a conductor passes through a magnetic field, a voltage is produced.
When there is a protrusion or no hole, the magnetic field is cut producing an output voltage, normally a HIGH.
When there is no protrusion or a hole, the magnetic field is not cut producing no output voltage, normally a LOW.
In other words, the moving object cuts or does not cut the magnetic field.
The HIGH to LOW transitions produce cycles that are measurable in electronic circuits.
When is a voltage produced in a magnetic pickup motion sensor?
When the conductor does not pass through the magnetic field.
When the applied voltage to the magnet changes.
When a conductor passes through the magnetic field.
Remember, it takes movement between a magnetic field and a conductor to produce voltage.
TRY AGAIN!
Electromagnetics use an applied voltage to produce the magnetic field. Changing the voltage only changes the strength of the field and does not produce an output voltage.
TRY AGAIN!
Finally, let's look at the correlation between motion and the frequency output of a motion sensor.
Note that any motion sensor can be used. We will use a photointerrupter in our example.
As the surface moves, the interrupter alternately senses the presence and absence of light.
This produces a square wave output of HIGHs and LOWs.
Compare the T times indicated on the sensor to the T times indicated on the square wave.
Look at the square wave. The cycle time from T1 to T3 depends on the speed (velocity) at which the wheel is turning.
Remember velocity equals the change in distance divided by the change in time.
Frequency equals one over time, velocity therefore is equal to distance times the frequency.
All that has to be done to find the velocity of the wheel is to measure the distance and multiply by the frequency output of the sensor.
This completes the information on SENSORS.E 1 TITLE........
1. Electronic motion sensors are devices that change velocity into frequency..
2. The photointerrupter uses light. The moving object makes or breaks the path of light to the light receiver..
3. The photoreflector also uses light. The moving object reflects or does not reflect the light to the light receiver.
4. The magnetic pickup uses magnetism. The moving object cuts or does not cut the magnetic field.
5. The output of any motion sensor is a square wave in which frequency is proportional to the velocity.
6. The velocity of an object is equal to the distance between sense points times the frequency output..

MOTION SENSOR CIRCUITS
Motion circuits are used to change the output of a motion sensor to a usable form.
DISCUSSION
By changing the frequency output of a motion sensor to voltage, a voltmeter can be scaled to indicate velocity.
If velocity is known another circuit can be added to indicate change in velocity (acceleration, deceleration).
Let's look at three circuits used to produce outputs representing.
The velocity circuit is used to change the frequency output of a motion sensor to an analog DC voltage.
The circuit consists of the motion sensor, amplifier/waveshaper and a frequency to voltage converter.
The motion sensor is a photointerrupter. Note that any motion sensor could have been used.
A slotted disk is used to interrupt the light from the LED to the phototransistor, P Q ..
The output voltage of the chip, E , depends on the frequency input and the conversion factor, CF.
The output of the phototransistor is then amplified and shaped in A1.
A2 is a frequency to DC voltage converter (F/V), normally an IC chip.
The converter produces a DC voltage output in proportion to the frequency input.
Note the SCALER IN and ZERO IN inputs to the F/V.
The inputs are used to scale the frequency to voltage conversion so that the chip may operate with any type of sensor.
Finally, by connecting a scaled voltmeter on the DC
output, you can obtain a direct reading of velocity.ity.

The next circuit to study is the acceleration circuit......
An acceleration circuit is nothing more than a velocity circuit with the addition of a differentiator circuit.
DIFFERENTIATOR CIRCUIT - A differentiator circuit is a RC circuit with the output taken across the capacitor.
DEFINITION
The acceleration circuit uses the same components as the velocity circuit (sensor, A1, A2).
A3 is the additional circuit, an op-amp differentiator, that is added to produce an output for acceleration or deceleration.M
With a constant DC voltage in (no change in velocity) the input capacitor blocks the constant DC voltage.
If there is no change in velocity (no acceleration or deceleration) the output of the op-amp is 0 volts.
If velocity increases, the DCV input increases.
C will then charge according to the RC time constant rate
Current will flow to the op-amp's inverting input producing a negative output since the non-inverting input is grounded.
Eout is a negative voltage that represents an increase in velocity...
If the velocity decreases, the DCV input decreases.
Cin will then discharge according to the RC rate (Cin times Rf)...
Current will flow out of the op-amp's inverting input producing a positive output.
Eout is a positive voltage that represents any decrease in velocity.
